clue.text: Get stricter reporting on match: "Ahead by a big margin"

indicators.note: a reporter's words are heard, so the word for a match is taken as spoken

parts.note: a match that ends level is a tie
a side leading by ten points or goals is ten up

explanation.surface: A sports report announces a runaway lead, oddly paired with a call for stricter rules.
explanation.walkthrough: TIE is said aloud and written TIGH; 'reporting' signals the sound. TEN UP is a big lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make rules or control firmer is to make them stricter.

clue.text: The lassie is not even a flirt

indicators.note: not even picks the odd-placed letters of the lassie

explanation.surface: A lassie is accused of being a flirt, and she is not even sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who leads others on playfully is a flirt.

clue.text: Ill-informed judgments have visitors losing time around the Home Counties

indicators.note: around says the shortened visitors wrap the region
losing says the time abbreviation is dropped from the visitors

parts.note: guests are visitors
the Home Counties are the counties around London, in south-east England, SE

explanation.surface: Visitors arriving late around the Home Counties make poor judgments.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties that surround London, in the south-east (SE).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: estimates made without full information are guesses.

clue.text: Heartless teenager in meal featuring tropical fish

indicators.note: in puts the outer letters of teenager inside the meal

parts.note: tea is an evening meal in Britain

indicators.note: heartless leaves only the outside letters of teenager

explanation.surface: A heartless teenager serves tropical fish for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain tea can be a light evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small colourful freshwater fish kept in home aquariums.

clue.text: Boy and not boy

parts.note: nor means and not
Bert is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Boy and not boy, a riddling contradiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a male first name stands for any boy.

clue.text: Party leader built up a fabrication to provide security

indicators.note: the leader of party is its opening letter
fabrication means making up, so the letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A party leader inflates a lie to give the country security.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: paying money as surety for an accused person's release secures their return to court.

clue.text: Girl, to become wife, runs out

indicators.note: out says the runs go missing from the word for wedding

parts.note: a woman becomes a wife when she weds
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A girl about to be wed runs off at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes R (runs) from MARRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a common female first name stands for any girl.

clue.text: Boatman's really odd, being neither animal nor vegetable

parts.note: Boatman is the setter, so Boatman's means the setter's own

indicators.note: odd picks the odd-placed letters of really

explanation.surface: The setter admits to being really odd, neither animal nor vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often call themselves by their pseudonym, so 'Boatman's' is 'mine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the parlour game Animal, Vegetable or Mineral names the third kingdom, things neither living nor plant.

clue.text: For cultivation, ordering a New World flower

indicators.note: for cultivation suggests the letters are worked like soil into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Ordering a New World flower for the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: A flower is a river (something that flows), not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword sense: a flower is something that flows, and this great American river runs between the USA and Mexico.

clue.text: East Germany without any changes for the better

indicators.note: without says the letters of the word any are taken away from the pool
changes says the remaining letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: East Germany, left unchanged, is said to be no better off.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A, N, Y from EASTGERMANY and rearrange the remaining letters ('without' and 'changes'). 'the better' means one who bets, not 'improved'.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword sense: a better is a person who places bets, and a gamester is a gambler.

clue.text: Girl overwhelmed by rattle — perhaps it makes a loud noise

definitions.text: perhaps it makes a loud noise

indicators.note: overwhelmed by puts the girl's name inside the word for a plaything

parts.note: a baby's rattle is a toy
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A small girl is drowned out by the din of her rattle.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tannoy is a British brand of public-address loudspeaker, used generically in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a public-address loudspeaker system booms announcements, hence 'perhaps' for one loud thing.

clue.text: Perhaps girl dancing in cage is harlot?

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words cage is harlot

explanation.surface: Is a girl dancing in a cage a harlot? asks a prudish observer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lifted from caGE IS HArlot. A geisha is not a harlot, so the surface's slur is a misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Japanese hostess trained to entertain with dance and music is one kind of dancing girl.

clue.text: People like Nero in Rome, always heading back after gold

indicators.note: heading back after says the leading letter of the Latin word moves to the rear, beyond the metal

parts.note: semper is Latin, the language of Rome, for always
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Romans like Nero always ran back for their gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Semper is Latin for always, signalled by 'in Rome'; 'heading back after' sends its head letter to the rear, past the gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Nero ruled Rome as one of its imperial rulers.

clue.text: Girl and boy married with prayer book

parts.note: a miss is a young girl
Al is a boy's name, short for Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: A girl and boy are wed with a prayer book in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a Catholic book of the Mass texts and prayers.

clue.text: One who digs heavy metal in club, either boy or girl, say

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

indicators.note: say signals the word for a youngster is taken as spoken

parts.note: a minor is a child of either sex

explanation.surface: A child at a club, boy or girl, is a heavy metal fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs heavy metal' looks like a music fan; it is mining for ore.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a worker who extracts the ore of a heavy metallic element from the ground.

clue.text: Translated article about principal of using barrels to deliver oil

indicators.note: about says the reworked article wraps the letters that follow
translated means the letters of article are rendered in a new form
the principal letter of using is its first

explanation.surface: A translated article on using barrels to deliver oil.
explanation.walkthrough: LRICATE (article shuffled, 'Translated') goes 'about' U (first of using) and B (barrels).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: as verbs, both mean to grease a mechanism so it runs smoothly.

clue.text: Boatman might try this to catch girl: "Want to get excited?"

definitions.text: Boatman might try this to catch

indicators.note: letters that get excited are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A boatman tries a chat-up line on a girl: want to get excited?
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is the setter, but here a boatman is a fisherman dragging a net.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: dragging a big net behind a boat is how a fishing crew catches its haul.

clue.text: Boy slips out, perhaps

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of place and rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy slips out, maybe, when nobody is looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both words express that something may be so.

clue.text: Boy makes move in dance with girl

parts.note: a step is a move in a dance
hen is informal for a woman or girl

explanation.surface: A boy makes a move on the dance floor with a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a male first name stands for any boy.

clue.text: "The young get nutrients from this cola" — Sky broadcast

definitions.text: The young get nutrients from this

indicators.note: broadcast scatters the letters widely into a new order

explanation.surface: A satellite channel advert claims youngsters get their nutrients from cola.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British broadcaster, so 'broadcast' feels like television.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an embryo draws its nourishment from the sac of yolk attached to it.

clue.text: Boy that is getting backing for Votes for Women

parts.note: a lad is a boy
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: the backing for a word is its rear end, its last letter

explanation.surface: A boy campaigns in support of Votes for Women, the suffragette slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a polite term for women in general.

clue.text: Boy, handy without being challenging

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside puts the handy word around the boy

parts.note: deft means skilful, handy
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy is handy without being difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: openly resisting authority is challenging it.

clue.text: August: one month before April, unusually around end of June

indicators.note: before puts the numeral and month in front of what follows

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: around says the reworked month wraps the single letter from June
unusually says the letters of April are arranged out of their normal order
end of picks the final letter of June

explanation.surface: A calendar puzzle: August comes one month before April, strangely, near the end of June.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIAL (April shuffled, 'unusually') goes 'around' E (end of June), giving PERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: august as an adjective means majestic and stately, like an emperor.

clue.text: As a married woman, her organisation procures an end to injustice in damsel, perhaps

parts.note: the WI, Women's Institute, is a British women's organisation

indicators.note: in puts the single letter inside the insect

parts.note: a damselfly is one kind of fly

indicators.note: an end to takes the closing letter of injustice

explanation.surface: A wife's women's group ends an injustice done to a damsel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British women's club; a damselfly is one kind of fly, hence 'perhaps'. 'an end to' takes the last letter of injustice, and 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: behaving as a wife does, in the manner of a married woman.

clue.text: Girl, to become wife, keeps name at end of ceremony

indicators.note: keeps says the verb for marrying holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: to wed is to become a wife

indicators.note: at end of picks the final letter of ceremony

explanation.surface: A girl about to wed keeps her name at the end of the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a female first name stands for any girl.

clue.text: Fastened shoes with raised design

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a decal is a transferred design

explanation.surface: Shoes were tied up, decorated with a raised pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised design' suggests embossing, but 'raised' turns DECAL upward in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tying up footwear by its strings is fastening it.

clue.text: Girl seen in series of articles

parts.note: the series opens with the indefinite article in its form before a vowel
the series continues with the definite article
the series closes with the indefinite article in its short form

explanation.surface: A girl appears in a series of newspaper features.
explanation.walkthrough: The articles here are grammar words, not newspaper pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a female first name, standing for any girl.

clue.text: Native American ritual for boy, say, and reformed church

indicators.note: say signals the word for a boy is taken as spoken

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: reformed says the letters of and are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A Native American ceremony for a boy, plus a reformed church.
explanation.walkthrough: DNA comes from 'and' shuffled ('reformed'); CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Plains Indian religious ceremony held at midsummer.

clue.text: Foremost of girl's relatives always nurturing

definitions.text: Foremost of girl's relatives always nurturing

indicators.note: foremost of takes the leading letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Of all a girl's relatives, the most nurturing is the one at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a grandmother is a relative traditionally seen as always caring for grandchildren.

clue.text: New in! Percy worked with another boy to put into code

indicators.note: worked means the letters are worked over into a new shape

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Percy and another boy work on putting a message into code.
explanation.walkthrough: N and PERCY are shuffled together ('worked') to give ENCRYP.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a message converted into cipher has been coded.
